monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity significantly this month while slightly reducing volume, reflected in faster paces, higher HR, and elevated time in Zones 3–5 — a clear shift toward threshold and VO2 max work.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 3–5 time jumped from 49% last month to 59% this month — indicating a strong, intentional shift toward higher-intensity work despite fewer runs.

goal_tracker.message: You need 12.6 more km across 3 sessions in the remaining 15 days to match last month’s volume — averaging ~4.2 km per session.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.28 to 13.62 km/hr per bpm this month, even as average HR increased +7 bpm and Zone 3–5 time grew — suggesting better cardiovascular economy at higher loads.

insights.title: Over-reliance on Zone 3–4 with minimal Z1 recovery
insights.body: Zone 1 dropped to just 11% this month (vs 4% last month), but remains critically low — only 11% of total training time is truly easy/recovery-focused, risking cumulative fatigue.

insights.title: Cadence stable but stride length and vertical oscillation vary widely
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 70.96 cm (April 1 long run) to 90.77 cm (April 12 hard run), and vertical oscillation varied between 7.8–8.5 cm — suggesting inconsistent form under fatigue or pace changes.

insights.title: High aerobic TE without proportional volume support
insights.body: Your April 12 run delivered 4.6 aerobic TE at 5.0 km and 7:25/km pace — your highest single-session TE this month — yet it followed only one other run in the prior 4 days, limiting recovery capacity for repeated high-TE efforts.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a strict 45-min Zone 2 effort (HR ≤138 bpm) at 8:30–9:00/km pace, aiming for ≥80% of time in Z2 per Garmin
recommendations.reason: Zone 1 is critically underutilized (11% this month) and Z2 dropped to 30% — you need a true recovery stimulus to restore autonomic balance and support upcoming intensity.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3×3-min progressive tempo run on flat terrain: start at 7:45/km (Z3), then 7:25/km (Z4), then 7:05/km (Z4–Z5 boundary), with 90-sec walk/jog recovery between reps
recommendations.reason: Your best recent pace is 7:25/km (445 sec/km) and you’ve spent 24% of time in Z4 — this bridges your current Z4 capacity with sustainable VO2 max exposure.

recommendations.action: Add 2x 60-sec barefoot strides on grass post-run (after your next two easy runs), focusing on quiet footstrike and cadence ≥160 spm
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time increased to 311 ms on your April 8 run (vs 301 ms on March 29), and vertical oscillation remains elevated — neuromuscular retraining will improve efficiency.

weekly_focus.description: Balance your recent surge in Z3–Z5 work with deliberate low-HR volume and targeted neuromuscular priming — rebuild aerobic resilience while preserving hard-earned speed gains.
